children: OTTAWA--Canadian manufacturing activity pulled back in July for the first time in six months as drops in chemical and food sales offset a rise in petroleum trade with higher prices.

Factory shipments declined 0.4% from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 78.71 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$56.75 billion, Statistics Canada said Monday. The drop was sharper than the data agency's early estimate for a decline of 0.2%.
Compared with a year earlier, sales were up 10.9%.
Sales in volume terms were down 1.4% for the month to C$54.0 billion, but up 0.4% on the same month last year.
